Preventive Maintenance Manual - TX-200 CNC Turning Centre
Document No. MNT-MAN-CNC-02 Revision 02
Effective Date 20-Jan-2026 Page See footer
Prepared By S. Arun, Maintenance Engineer Approved By V. Ramesh, Maintenance Manager
1. Purpose
This manual defines the preventive maintenance (PM) activities, operating parameters and common alarms
for the TX-200 CNC turning centres (machines CNC-04 to CNC-09) used on the shaft machining line. 2. Safety First
Before starting any maintenance activity other than daily operator checks, the machine must be isolated as
per SAF-SOP-003 Lockout/Tagout. Never open the electrical cabinet or hydraulic circuit on a running or
energised machine. 3. Normal Operating Parameters

5. Chuck Mounting Bolt Torque
When re-mounting the chuck after maintenance, tighten the mounting bolts in a criss-cross sequence to 110
Nm using a calibrated torque wrench. 6. Common Alarms

maintenance if repeated. AL-305 Spindle overload Stop cycle. Check tool wear and cutting parameters. Inform shift

1. Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure. 2. Confirm the panel pressure gauge reads zero before loosening any fitting. 3. Place a drip tray under the hose and loosen the fittings slowly. 4. Fit a new hose of the same rating and tighten fittings. 5. Remove locks as per SAF-SOP-003, start the hydraulic unit and confirm pressure returns to 3. 5 - 4.

Kaveri Precision Components Pvt. Ltd. - Hosur Plant
Incoming Material Inspection - Standard Operating Procedure
Document No. QC-SOP-014 Revision 03
Effective Date 15-Mar-2023 Page See footer
Prepared By R. Selvam, QC Engineer Approved By M. Prakash, QC Manager
1. Purpose
This procedure describes how incoming raw materials and bought-out components are inspected at the
receiving area before they are released to stores and production. 2. Scope
Applies to all steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components received at the Hosur plant. 3. Responsibilities
•  Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against the delivery challan and informs QC. •  QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results. •  QC Supervisor: approves acceptance or rejection of the lot. 4. Procedure
1.

Procedure
1. Stores Executive places the received lot in the Incoming Inspection Area and raises an inspection
request. 2. QC Inspector collects the purchase order, drawing and supplier test certificate (if available). 3. Draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size. 4. Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs. 5. Perform dimensional inspection on all critical dimensions using a vernier caliper. 6. If all 5 samples are within specification, the lot is accepted. If any sample fails, the complete lot is
rejected. 7. Record results on paper form QF-07 Incoming Inspection Report and file it in the QC office. 8. Accepted material is tagged with a GREEN tag and moved to stores. 9. Rejected material is tagged with a RED tag and kept in the Red Bin area near Gate 2 until it is returned
to the supplier. 10. QC Supervisor informs Purchase by email about rejected lots by end of the shift. 5.

5. Records
•  QF-07 Incoming Inspection Report (paper) - retained for 2 years. 6. Revision History
Rev Date Change
01 10-Jan-2019 First issue
02 05-Aug-2021 Added visual inspection criteria
03 15-Mar-2023 Changed sample size to 5 for all lots

Incoming Material Inspection - Standard Operating Procedure
Document No. QC-SOP-014 Revision 04
Effective Date 01-Jul-2026 Page See footer
Prepared By K. Divya, Supplier Quality Engineer Approved By M. Prakash, QC Manager
1. Purpose
This procedure describes how incoming raw materials and bought-out components are inspected at the
receiving area before they are released to stores and production. 2. Scope
Applies to all steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components received at the Hosur plant,
including machined BH-220 bearing housings received from sub-contractors. 3. Responsibilities
•  Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against the delivery challan and raises the
inspection request in the QMS app.

•  QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results in the QMS
app. •  Shift QC Supervisor: approves acceptance, rejection or hold of the lot. •  Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE): handles supplier communication for rejected or held lots. 4. Sampling Plan
Defects are classified as follows:
•  Critical: a defect that can cause a safety risk or failure of the part, e. g. crack, wrong material grade, or a
dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Critical. •  Major: a defect that affects fit or function but is not critical, e. g. deep dent, damaged thread, or a
dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Major. •  Minor: a cosmetic defect that does not affect fit or function, e. g. light surface marks or light surface rust
that can be removed by cleaning. The number of samples depends on the lot size. Minor defects are allowed only as shown below.

Minor defects are allowed only as shown below. Lot size (pieces) Samples to inspect Accept if minor defects are Reject if minor defects are
2 - 5 All pieces 0 1 or more
6 - 90 5 0 1 or more
91 - 500 13 0 1 or more
501 - 3,200 32 1 or fewer 2 or more
Above 3,200 50 2 or fewer 3 or more
Any critical defect in any sample: the complete lot is rejected and returned to the supplier. Sorting is not
allowed. Any major defect in any sample: the complete lot is rejected. The SQE may decide to have the lot 100%
sorted at the supplier's cost instead of returning it. 5. Procedure

QC-SOP-014  |  Rev 04  |  Uncontrolled copy when printed. Refer to QMS for the latest version. Page 2
1. Stores Executive places the received lot in the Incoming Inspection Area and raises an inspection request
in the QMS app. 2. QC Inspector checks that the supplier's Material Test Certificate (MTC) is attached. The MTC is
mandatory. If it is missing, the lot is put on HOLD and must not be inspected or accepted until the MTC is
received. 3. Draw samples at random as per the sampling plan in Section 4. 4. Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs. 5. Perform dimensional inspection using a calibrated digital caliper. Dimensions of BH-220 housings marked
CMM in Section 6 must be checked on the CMM. 6. Record results in the QMS app using digital form QF-07A. Paper form QF-07 is no longer used. 7. Accepted material is tagged with a GREEN tag and moved to stores. 8. Rejected material is tagged with a RED tag and moved to Quarantine Cage Q1, Stores Bay 3.

Rejected material is tagged with a RED tag and moved to Quarantine Cage Q1, Stores Bay 3. The cage
is locked; the key is held by the Shift QC Supervisor. 9. The Shift QC Supervisor must inform the SQE within 4 hours of rejection. The SQE raises a Supplier
Corrective Action Request (SCAR). 6. Inspection Dimensions - BH-220 Bearing Housing (Machined, from
sub-contractor)

•  QF-07A Incoming Inspection Report (digital, in QMS app) - retained for 5 years.

SAF-SOP-003  |  Rev 05  |  Uncontrolled copy when printed. Refer to QMS for the latest version. Page 1
Kaveri Precision Components Pvt. Ltd. - Hosur Plant
Lockout / Tagout (LOTO) - Safety Procedure
Document No. SAF-SOP-003 Revision 05
Effective Date 12-Feb-2026 Page See footer
Prepared By J. Fathima, Safety Officer Approved By A. Krishnan, Plant Head
1. Purpose
To protect people from the unexpected start-up of machines or release of stored energy (electrical, hydraulic,
pneumatic, mechanical) during maintenance, cleaning, setting or repair. 2. Scope
Applies to all employees and contract workers at the Hosur plant who maintain, clean or repair machines,
including CNC turning centres, presses and compressors. 3. Definitions
•  Authorised person: a trained employee who applies their own personal lock and tag to isolate energy. •  Affected person: an operator or employee who works in the area but does not perform the isolation.

•  Affected person: an operator or employee who works in the area but does not perform the isolation. •  Zero energy state: the condition where all energy sources are isolated and stored energy is released, so
that the machine cannot move or release energy. 4. Lockout Procedure
1. Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance. 2. Stop the machine using the normal stop sequence. 3. Isolate all energy sources: main electrical isolator, compressed air valve, and hydraulic power unit. 4. Apply your personal red lock and danger tag to each isolation point. Each authorised person working
on the machine applies their own lock. Use a multi-lock hasp when more than one person is involved. 5. Release stored energy: bleed hydraulic pressure and accumulators until the gauge reads zero, vent
compressed air to 0 bar, and block any parts that can fall under gravity. 6.

6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine from the control panel and confirm it does not start. Confirm
all pressure gauges read zero. Return controls to OFF. 5. Removing Locks
1. Check that tools and materials are removed and guards are refitted. 2. Confirm all persons are clear of the machine. 3. Each authorised person removes only their own lock. Nobody may remove another person's lock. 4. Inform affected persons that the machine is being restarted. 6. Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent
If an authorised person has left the plant without removing their lock, the lock may be removed only through
this procedure:
1. The Shift Supervisor makes every reasonable effort to contact the lock owner by phone. 2. If the owner cannot be reached, the Production Manager and the Safety Officer must both authorise
removal. 3. The machine is physically inspected to confirm it is safe to re-energise.

SAF-SOP-003  |  Rev 05  |  Uncontrolled copy when printed. Refer to QMS for the latest version. Page 2
4. The removal is recorded on form SF-12 Lock Removal Record. 5. The lock owner must be informed before they resume work on their next shift. 7. Training and Audits
•  All authorised persons must complete LOTO training before applying locks, with refresher training every
12 months. •  The Safety Officer audits LOTO practice on each shift at least once a month. •  Violation of this procedure is treated as a serious safety breach.
